Chile.name: Atacama Desert
Chile.note: Driest non-polar desert on Earth; some weather stations have never recorded rain.

Argentina.name: Pampas
Argentina.note: Fertile grassland plains — the agricultural heartland of Argentina (beef, wheat, soy).

Argentina.name: Patagonia
Argentina.note: Windswept semi-arid plateau/steppe spanning southern Argentina and Chile.

Bolivia.name: Altiplano
Bolivia.note: High Andean plateau (~3,750 m average), second-largest after the Tibetan Plateau.

Paraguay.name: Gran Chaco
Paraguay.note: Vast lowland plain of scrub and grassland, shared with Argentina and Bolivia.

United States.name: Great Plains
United States.note: Vast interior grassland — the US/Canada 'breadbasket', once home to vast bison herds.

United States.name: Colorado Plateau
United States.note: High sedimentary plateau carved by rivers into the Grand Canyon.

United States.name: Mojave Desert
United States.note: Home to Death Valley, the hottest and lowest point in North America.

Mexico.name: Sonoran Desert
Mexico.note: Shared with the southwestern US; known for the iconic saguaro cactus.

Canada.name: Canadian Prairies
Canada.note: Wheat-growing plains across Alberta, Saskatchewan and Manitoba.

Algeria.name: Sahara Desert
Algeria.note: World's largest hot desert, spanning most of North Africa across ~11 countries.

Kenya.name: East African savanna
Kenya.note: Grassland/savanna supporting the Great Migration across the Serengeti–Mara ecosystem.

Ethiopia.name: Ethiopian Highlands
Ethiopia.note: 'Roof of Africa' — source of the Blue Nile, shaped by the Great Rift Valley.

South Africa.name: Kalahari Desert
South Africa.note: Semi-arid sandy savanna spanning South Africa, Botswana and Namibia.

South Africa.name: Highveld
South Africa.note: High interior plateau (~1,500 m) where Johannesburg and Pretoria sit.

Ukraine.name: Pontic Steppe
Ukraine.note: Fertile black-soil (chernozem) grassland — historic invasion corridor and grain belt.

Spain.name: Meseta Central
Spain.note: High interior plateau covering much of Spain, where Madrid sits.

Norway.name: Scandinavian Mountains (fjord plateau)
Norway.note: Glacially carved highlands behind Norway's fjord coastline.

Saudi Arabia.name: Rub' al Khali (Empty Quarter)
Saudi Arabia.note: Largest contiguous sand desert in the world.

Mongolia.name: Gobi Desert
Mongolia.note: Cold desert spanning southern Mongolia and northern China.

China.name: Tibetan Plateau
China.note: 'Roof of the World' (~4,500 m average) — source of Asia's major rivers.

Kazakhstan.name: Kazakh Steppe
Kazakhstan.note: One of the world's largest dry steppe regions, historic Silk Road corridor.

India.name: Thar Desert
India.note: Great Indian Desert along the India–Pakistan border, in Rajasthan.

India.name: Deccan Plateau
India.note: Triangular volcanic plateau covering most of peninsular India.

Australia.name: Great Victoria Desert
Australia.note: Australia's largest desert, spanning Western Australia and South Australia.

Australia.name: Nullarbor Plain
Australia.note: Vast, almost treeless limestone plateau along the southern coast.
